# Protected computation controlled by grade boundaries, not a global noise norm

Root construction, 29 October 2026. New representation; independent review recorded separately. Earlier energy-window results remain valid at their pinned scope. Their conservation and retirement premises are sufficient for that method, not necessities for every protected operation.

## 1. The consequential change

The graded proof propagates all motion inside a grade, and all motion after escape, unitarily. Only the edges between successive grades and the final escape edge need norm estimates. A bosonic interaction may therefore be globally unbounded, and actual occupations may grow without a uniform ceiling, while the protected operation still has a finite complete-channel error bound.

## 2. General edge theorem

Let \(P_0,\ldots,P_q,Q\) be orthogonal projectors summing to identity, with \(P=\sum_rP_r\). Memory is included in every sector. Assume the block-diagonal dynamics has normalized unitary propagators on these sectors. Add bounded, strongly measurable, locally integrable edges
\[
K_r(t)=P_rH(t)P_{r-1}\ (1\le r\le q),\qquad
K_{q+1}(t)=QH(t)P_q
\tag{1}
\]
and their adjoints, with no other off-diagonal edges. Define the physical evolution by this bounded interaction-picture perturbation of the direct-sum propagator. The comparison removes only \(K_{q+1}+K_{q+1}^\dagger\). Both are normalized. This specification handles unbounded diagonal generators without relying on formal block matrix elements or changing self-adjoint domains.

Set \(e_r(t)=\|K_r(t)\|\). Then, uniformly on the complete fresh input \(P_0\), including memory and references,
\[
\|(U(b,a)-\bar U(b,a))P_0\|
\le\int_{a<t_1<\cdots<t_{q+1}<b}
\prod_{r=1}^{q+1}e_r(t_r)\,dt_1\cdots dt_{q+1}.
\tag{2}
\]
For a common envelope \(e_r(t)\le h(t)\), with \(\Theta=\int_a^bh(t)dt\),
\[
\boxed{\ \|(U-\bar U)P_0\|\le
\Theta^{q+1}/(q+1)!\ }.
\tag{3}
\]
The complete-channel half-diamond distance is at most the minimum of one and this bound.

\[

\le\int_a^t e_r(s)\|P_{r-1}\bar U(s,a)P_0\|\,ds.
\]

Author: producer-workspace/classical_capacity, 2026-10-29.

This is a separate authored addendum. The accepted main note, CONSTRUCTIVE_FINE_READOUT.md, and its proof, executable, data, receipt and independent review remain unchanged. Root requested independent review of this addendum after construction.

## 1. The operation being certified

The full fine-count comparison in the main note asks that every detected count match the count of an ideal detector. A final computing output need not demand that operation. Here the reference is **a correct logical Z result or an explicit erasure flag, with the same actual raw counts and the same count-conditioned retained memory as the real detector**.

On the entire admitted logical-times-syndrome space, one missed photon cannot cause an accepted wrong logical result. It may cause an erasure flag. Consequently the complete error relative to this correct-or-flag operation is bounded by a two-miss tail, while the declared erasure probability remains a separately charged first-order cost. The result holds for arbitrary coherent syndrome inputs, correlations with retained memory and references.

The port is exactly the main note's equal-efficiency independent vacuum attenuation followed by ideal mode-resolved destructive counting. The uncollected fields and any environment needed to make the stated record classical are genuinely retired at the declared interface. This is not a certificate for a returning loss-field purification, a general noisy detector, or an always-success readout.

Let q>=1, L=q+1, N=L^2 and n_max=N+q. Let

\[
J:L_{\rm log}\otimes S\longrightarrow A
\]

\[

\qquad
\sum_{\nu:\ell_\nu=\ell}|v_\nu\rangle\langle v_\nu|=I_S .
\tag{1}
\]

## Completed: protection governed by the transitions that can carry information out

I pursued a stronger question than extending the eraser: **can protected gates and repeated transfer to fresh encodings remain certifiable when a driven, returning bath gives the physical oscillator unbounded energy support?**

The resulting **bounded-edge protection principle** answers yes at an explicit interaction and control interface. It removes the global noise-norm and invariant-cutoff obstruction encountered in the earlier representation. Both the functional-analysis review and the separate driven-bath/returning-memory challenge accepted the construction at its stated scope.

### The principle

Arrange the protected space into error grades \(P_0,\ldots,P_q\), with \(P_0\) the fresh encoding. Suppose the interaction moves only between adjacent grades, and escape requires crossing the final boundary. Bound those transitions while propagating the motion within each grade—and beyond the protected boundary—unitarily.

For a common edge-norm envelope whose integral over block \(j\)’s **whole physical lifetime** is \(\Theta_j\), the complete-channel comparison satisfies

\[
\boxed{
\epsilon_{\mathrm{dyn}}
\le
\min\!\left\{1,\;
\sum_j\frac{\Theta_j^{\,q_j+1}}{(q_j+1)!}
\right\}.
}
\]

The comparison includes the retained bath, retired blocks and arbitrary references on the declared encoded input domain. Holding and handoff exposure count. An already occupied syndrome cannot obtain a fresh protection order merely by restarting a clock.

The proof follows successive incoming sources through the grades. Once amplitude escapes, its subsequent evolution has norm one; its Hamiltonian need not have a finite global norm. A sharper theorem retains the actual time-ordered edge integral.
